record.reply:
The objection notes that my earlier argument used "expected survivors" (0.95 vs 0.05) as the decisive metric, whereas classical utilitarianism seeks to maximise total expected welfare, not merely survival counts.  

1  Admitted facts supporting the bridge  
• PROP:WORLD:E2 – Ben’s survival probability is 5 %.  
• PROP:WORLD:E4 – Cara’s survival probability is 95 %.  
Both patients face certain death otherwise (PROP:WORLD:E7, E8).  

2  Framework commitment  
Utilitarianism ranks actions by their expected utility.  In many urgent medical triage cases, continued life for someone who would otherwise die is taken as the dominant welfare component; when the patients are unknown to us and no further quality-of-life differences are supplied, a one-life-year proxy (or simple life/not-life proxy) is the least‐controversial common unit.  Under that simplifying assumption “expected survivors” becomes a direct proxy for expected utility.  

3  Why the proxy is appropriate here  
• Symmetry: The n
record.framework_commitment: Using survival as a welfare proxy is justified when (a) the only material outcomes given are life or death, (b) no quality-of-life or preference differences are stated, and (c) each patient counts equally in Benthamite aggregation.  Under these conditions, maximising expected survivors is equivalent to maximising expected welfare.
record.reasoning_bridge: From PROP:WORLD:E2 and PROP:WORLD:E4 we derive expected utility contributions of 0.05 life and 0.95 life.  Because all other utilities are symmetrical or unspecified, the higher expected-life action (A1) yields greater total expected welfare.
record.remaining_uncertainty: If there were large, undisclosed differences in post-treatment quality of life, social roles, or the patients’ own preferences, survival counts might not track welfare precisely.  Those data are absent.
record.reversal_condition: If Ben’s probability of survival were to exceed Cara’s (e.g. > 95 %), the expected-survivor proxy would favour A0, reversing the recommendation.
